questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{1}[t],$ the vector space of real polynomials of degree at most $1,$ and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1).
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=2t,\,{p}_{2}(t)=t-1,\,q(t)=4t-3
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t)}$ equals $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,q(t)={\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t).
$$

We are given that ${\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)=t,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{2}(t)}.$ This can be computed as

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t)=\frac{⟨q(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩}{⟨{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩}\,{p}_{2}(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩ & =q(0){p}_{2}(0)+q(1){p}_{2}(1) \\  & =(4t-3){|}_{0}\cdot (t-1){|}_{0}+(4t-3){|}_{1}\cdot (t-1){|}_{1} \\  & =(-3)\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 0 \\  & =3,\end{aligned}
$$

  

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{p}_{2}(t),{p}_{2}(t)⟩ & ={p}_{2}(0){p}_{2}(0)+{p}_{2}(1){p}_{2}(1) \\  & =(t-1)^{2}{|}_{0}+(t-1)^{2}{|}_{1} \\  & =(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t) & =\frac{3}{1}\cdot (t-1)=3t-3.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,q(t) & ={\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t) \\  & =t+(3t-3) \\  & =4t-3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t],$ the vector space of real polynomials of degree at most $2,$ and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1).
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=t,\,{p}_{2}(t)={t}^{2}-1,\,q(t)={t}^{2}+t
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${p}_{1}(t)⊥{p}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{2}(t)}$ equals $0.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,q(t)={\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t).
$$

We are given that ${\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t)=0,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $q(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{p}_{1}(t)}.$ This can be computed as

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)=\frac{⟨q(t),{p}_{1}(t)⟩}{⟨{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{1}(t)⟩}\,{p}_{1}(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨q(t),{p}_{1}(t)⟩ & =q(-1){p}_{1}(-1)+q(0){p}_{1}(0)+q(1){p}_{1}(1) \\  & =({t}^{2}\,+\,t){|}_{-1}\,\,\cdot \,(t){|}_{-1}+({t}^{2}\,+\,t){|}_{0}\,\,\cdot \,(t){|}_{0}+({t}^{2}\,+\,t){|}_{1}\,\,\cdot \,(t){|}_{1} \\  & =0\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 0+2\cdot 1 \\  & =2,\end{aligned}
$$

  

and

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{1}(t)⟩ & ={p}_{1}(-1){p}_{1}(-1)+{p}_{1}(0){p}_{1}(0)+{p}_{1}(1){p}_{1}(1) \\  & =(t)^{2}{|}_{-1}+(t)^{2}{|}_{0}+(t)^{2}{|}_{1} \\  & =(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t) & =\frac{2}{2}\cdot t=t.\end{aligned}
$$

  

Finally,  

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,q(t) & ={\text{proj}}_{{p}_{1}(t)}\,q(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{p}_{2}(t)}\,q(t) \\  & =t+0 \\  & =t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[-1,1],$ the vector space of continuous functions over $[-1,1]$, and let the inner product on $V$ be defined as

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{-1}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Now consider the following elements of $V:$ 

$$
{f}_{1}(t)=3t,\,{f}_{2}(t)={t}^{2}+1,\,g(t)=10{t}^{3}
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $S=\text{Span}{{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t)}$ given that ${f}_{1}(t)⊥{f}_{2}(t)$ with respect to the inner product, and that the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{f}_{1}(t)}$ equals $6t.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{f}_{1}(t),{f}_{2}(t)}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t)={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t).
$$

We are given that ${\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)=6t,$ so let's now find the orthogonal projection of $g(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{{f}_{2}(t)}.$ This can be computed as

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t)=\frac{⟨g(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩}{⟨{f}_{2}(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩}\,{f}_{2}(t).
$$

 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨g(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}g(t){f}_{2}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}10{t}^{3}\cdot ({t}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}10{t}^{3}({t}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $10{t}^{3}$ is an odd function, while ${t}^{2}+1$ is even. Hence, their product $10{t}^{3}({t}^{2}+1)$ must be an odd function. Now, since we have an integral over the interval $[-1,1],$ which is symmetric about the origin, we can conclude that

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}10{t}^{3}({t}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}t=0.
$$

  

Therefore,

$$
{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t)=\frac{0}{⟨{f}_{2}(t),{f}_{2}(t)⟩}\cdot ({t}^{2}+1)=0.
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,g(t) & ={\text{proj}}_{{f}_{1}(t)}\,g(t)+{\text{proj}}_{{f}_{2}(t)}\,g(t) \\  & =6t+0 \\  & =6t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Vector and a Subspace
questions.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1],$ the vector space of functions that are continuous over $[0,1].$ Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t,
$$

find the distance between $f(t)=8t$ and the subspace spanned by $g(t)=4t-2$ with respect to the inner product.
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $f(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{g(t)}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t) & =\frac{⟨f(t),g(t)⟩}{⟨g(t),g(t)⟩}\,g(t) \\  & =\frac{{\int }_{0}^{1}8t\cdot (4t-2)\,\text{d}t}{{\int }_{0}^{1}(4t-2)^{2}\,\text{d}t}\cdot (4t-2) \\  & =\frac{{\int }_{0}^{1}(32{t}^{2}-16t)\,\text{d}t}{{\int }_{0}^{1}(16{t}^{2}-16t+4)\,\text{d}t}\cdot (4t-2) \\  & =\frac{[\frac{32}{3}{t}^{3}-8{t}^{2}]_{0}^{1}}{[\frac{16}{3}{t}^{3}-8{t}^{2}+4t]_{0}^{1}}\cdot (4t-2) \\  & =\frac{(\frac{32}{3}-8)-0}{(\frac{16}{3}-4)-0}\cdot (6t-3) \\  & =\frac{(\frac{8}{3})}{(\frac{4}{3})}\cdot (4t+2) \\  & =2\cdot (4t-2) \\  & =8t-4.\end{aligned}
$$

The distance between $f(t)=8t$ and the subspace spanned by $g(t)=4t-2$ with respect to our inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖f(t)-{\text{proj}}_{g(t)}\,f(t)‖ \\  & =‖8t-(8t-4)‖ \\  & =‖4‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨4,4⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨4,4⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4\cdot 4\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}16\,\text{d}t \\  & =16t\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =16-0 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d=\sqrt{16}=4.$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Vector and a Subspace
questions.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t],$ the vector space of polynomials of degree at most $2$ with real coefficients. Given that the inner product on $V$ is defined as 

$$
⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1),
$$

find the distance between $p(t)=5t$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t)=t-1$ with respect to the inner product.
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $p(t)$ onto $\text{Span}{q(t)}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t) & =\frac{⟨p(t),q(t)⟩}{⟨q(t),q(t)⟩}\,q(t) \\  & =\frac{p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1)}{q(-1)q(-1)+q(0)q(0)+q(1)q(1)}\cdot q(t) \\  & =\frac{{\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(5t){|}_{t=i}\cdot (t-1){|}_{t=i}}{{\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(t-1){|}_{t=i}\cdot (t-1){|}_{t=i}}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =\frac{(-5)\cdot (-2)+0\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 0}{(-2)\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot (-1)+0\cdot 0}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =\frac{10}{5}\cdot (t-1) \\  & =2(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

 

The distance between $p(t)=5t$ and the subspace spanned by $q(t)=t-1$ with respect to our inner product is

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =‖p(t)-{\text{proj}}_{q(t)}\,p(t)‖ \\  & =‖5t-2(t-1)‖ \\  & =‖3t+2‖ \\  & =\sqrt{⟨3t+2,3t+2⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the inner product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨3t+2,3t+2⟩ & ={\sum }_{i\in {-1,0,1}}(3t+2){|}_{t=i}\cdot (3t+2){|}_{t=i} \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)+2\cdot 2+5\cdot 5 \\  & =1+4+25 \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the distance is $d=\sqrt{30}.$
